shared_elements: T-shaped/rectangular carved stone block on a vertical shaft
upper register of repeated arched or looped motifs with small animals above them
horizontal band of dense zigzag/net-like patterning acting as a divider
row of quadrupeds in profile walking in a single direction
long-necked bird in profile on the lower shaft
shallow, flat-cut low relief on rough weathered stone
excavation context with surrounding rubble stones and earth
justification: Both stones repeat an unusually specific compositional scheme: a broad rectangular head bearing an upper strip of repeated arch-like motifs surmounted by small animals, a horizontal zigzag/net band beneath it, then a register of profile quadrupeds, with a long-necked bird and snake-like forms carved on the narrower shaft below. The main differences are the viewing angle (A upright and frontal, B tilted and foreshortened) and the greater crispness and detail of A's carving compared with B's flatter, more eroded surface, but the shared motif inventory, order and shallow flat relief technique point to the same workshop tradition.
